scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #9027: After a maintenance window, routes for the R7 region (17.x.x.x,
67.0.0.0/8, 70.0.0.0/8) vanished from R1's routing table and R6 lost its OSPF
neighbor R7. The team believes the R6<->R7 link (67.0.0.0/8) went down or was
unplugged during the maintenance. Please confirm the R6<->R7 link failure and
identify the down interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath5-r7-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R7. With its
ospfd stopped, R6 ages out R7's LSAs and the withdrawals propagate through area 1
and the backbone, so R1 loses the R7 region (17.x, 67.x, 70.x).

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed R6<->R7 link
(67.0.0.0/8). The link is actually UP and forwarding (R6 and R7 can still reach
each other's 67.x interface IPs); nothing physical failed. The "lost adjacency and
withdrawn prefixes" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a maintenance-window
link failure) is a red herring -- the routing daemon stopped, the wire did not.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r7 (ospfd not running). The
agent must check Layer 1/2 (the R6<->R7 link / 67.x interfaces are up), then the
routing daemon (ospfd dead on R7), and explicitly reject the "link down"
narrative. An agent that "confirms the down link" has followed the ticket's
framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on R7.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r7" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r7 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r7). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r7.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: OSPF control-plane on R7 (ospfd daemon) is down. The physical data-plane link between R6 and R7 is healthy.
- Mechanism: With ospfd not running on R7, R6 has no OSPF neighbor on the 67.0.0.0/8 segment, so R7’s routes (its loopbacks 17.x.x.x and LAN 70.0.0.0/8) are no longer advertised into the network. Consequently, R1 no longer has those routes. This appears as a “neighbor down” on R6 and vanished routes on R1.
- Localization: R6<->R7 link is the Y segment (R6 eth2 <-> R7 eth0). Evidence shows:
  • Physical/link up: ethtool reports “Link detected: yes” on R6 eth2 and R7 eth0. 
  • L3 reachability up: R6 can ping R7 at 67.1.1.2 with 0% loss.
  • OSPF adjacency down: R6 “show ip ospf neighbor” lists no neighbor on eth2; on R7, “ospfd is not running.”
  • Route loss at R1: “show ip route 17.0.0.0/8” and “70.0.0.0/8” return “Network not in table.” (67.0.0.0/8 is currently present via another OSPF path, likely learned via R6/R3, but R7-originated routes are missing.)
- Root cause: The ospfd process on R7 is stopped after the maintenance, not a cable or interface failure.
- Corrective fix: Restart and enable OSPF on R7 (e.g., systemctl restart frr; ensure ospfd is enabled in FRR daemons and interfaces 67.0.0.0/8 on eth0 and 70.0.0.0/8 on eth1 are in OSPF). Once ospfd is running, R6 will reestablish adjacency and R1 will relearn 17.x.x.x and 70.0.0.0/8. No interface is down; the link R6 eth2 <-> R7 eth0 is operational.

per_axis.rationale: Explicitly identifies the ospfd OSPF routing daemon on R7 as the failed component (ospfd not running).
The agent recommends restarting/enabling ospfd (FRR) on R7 and ensuring interfaces are in OSPF, which matches the expected remediation to restore adjacency and routes.

The agent's investigation log contains the key observations (interfaces UP, successful ping between R6/R7, ospfd not running on R7, missing routes on R1) that support the conclusion. The writeup's inferences follow logically and cover the necessary checks to reject a physical-link failure and identify the daemon outage as root cause.
